subject: Civil Engineering
title: Traffic Flow Theory
description: A 60-second lesson on Traffic Flow Theory.

hook.text: Traffic moves like fluid. Compress it too much and it stops — a jam forms.

buildup.text: Three variables define traffic: flow (vehicles per hour), density, and speed.

discovery.text: Flow equals density times speed. At maximum density, speed drops to zero — gridlock.

twist.text: Maximum flow happens at moderate density — not empty, not packed. The sweet spot.

climax.text: Greenshields' model describes this relationship — still used since 1935.

punchline.text: Traffic has physics, and engineers use it to design capacity.

quiz.question: What happens to traffic flow at maximum vehicle density?
options: Speed increases because drivers want to escape congestion
Speed drops to zero and flow stops — complete gridlock
Vehicles automatically reroute to parallel roads
